anchoredOn.pathNote: The spec cites studio-runner/src/guided/observationCollector.ts; the file is studio-runner/src/run/observationCollector.ts. Line 419 matches.

verifiedFacts: guidedConfig.ts:13 MOUNTED_KEYS contains 'rules'. s3-cutover.patch removes only 'applicationPolicy' and keeps 'rules' (patch lines 22-23).
guidedMain.ts:24 passes config.rules to createGuidedServer. guided/runtime.ts:108 puts this.options.rules into the collector's ObservationConfig.
observationCollector.ts:222-226 (resolveReadPolicy): an exact testId rule whose classification is not structuralOnly returns a ReadPolicy (visibleText or controlValue). This is read authorization.
observationCollector.ts:419: readPossible = rule.classification !== 'structuralOnly' when a rule exists. Governed readGrants are consulted only when no rule exists.
observationCollector.ts:427,433: a rule makes a node 'safe' without an applicationPolicy and sets the exported name, classification and policyRuleId.

The governed context forbids rules inside applicationPolicy. C2b fixture case: 'runner-context / context / /applicationPolicy/rules = [] / SCHEMA'. So a mounted rule is the only path for an exact field read, and nothing governs it.
AR-2 g (ar-2-3-obs014.json:170) states its design intent: 'learning origins/read rules then come from the governed object'.

Contrary to C2b's note 'not traced to a guided IT config': GuidedBridgeIntegrationTest.java:798-812 mounts read-granting rules (source permittedBusinessData, destination nonsecretApproved) for every test except configuredRegionReadGrantNeedsNoTestIdsOrPerControlRules and freshObservationConnectsTwoAuthoredStepsWithoutReplayingProducer (:714-734). studio-runner/test/run/guidedMain.test.ts:12 mounts a permittedBusinessData rule.
GuidedPlanningIntegrationTest.java:2832-2848 builds the same rules, but :2780 sets genericRead = true for every test, and :2850 then calls config.putArray("rules").
inferred: Jackson ObjectNode.putArray replaces an existing field, so GuidedPlanningIntegrationTest effectively mounts rules: []. This is API knowledge and was not run.

The collector's `rules` option is also fed by the replay path (validator/observedReferencePolicy.ts:285-289 projects TrustedPolicy.rules). The fix belongs at the guided worker boundary (guidedConfig/guidedMain/createGuidedServer/runtime), not in the collector. This was read in code, not traced end to end.

decision.ruling: IN SCOPE of STUDIO-OBS-014 AC-1, recorded as an AC-1 clarification (a-f) in the story. No new AC and no new story.
rationale: AC-1 lists the 'read rules' as part of the governed ObservationApplicationPolicy, and requires the runner to validate the hash of 'the policy it applies'. When a mounted rule grants a read, the applied read policy differs from the hashed policy, which empties the 'runner accepts only v2' oracle of meaning.

The panel finding behind AC-1 was that the read policy is a worker-mounted file with no owner, approval or audit. A mounted read-granting rule is the same defect. AC-1 names `applicationPolicy` only because that was the anchor at HEAD.

Moving it to the AC-2 R-2 two-policy-sources follow-up (C2b's candidate) would be wrong. R-2 concerns replay binding to TrustedPolicy. This is learning-path read authorization, and the R-2 follow-up is not release-blocking.
decision.requiredOutcome: After S3 the guided learning worker accepts no mounted file and no server option that (1) makes a node readable or resolves a read policy, (2) sets or changes an exported node's classification or policyRuleId, or (3) widens which nodes are exported, beyond the governed policy in the hash-bound runner context. A violation is CONFIGURATION_DENIED. Replay TrustedPolicy.rules are unchanged (R-2 interim).

forArchitect.question: What exact rule applies to mounted guided-worker `rules`?
forArchitect.poDefault: Remove 'rules' from MOUNTED_KEYS and refuse the key in every form, including []. createGuidedServer refuses a `rules` option that is not empty, or drops the option. The guided runtime builds the collector config with rules: [].
forArchitect.alternative: Allow only structuralOnly rules. This needs a stated rationale, because a structuralOnly rule still sets the exported name and policyRuleId from an ungoverned file (observationCollector.ts:433).
forArchitect.outOfScope: Exact testId field reads inside the governed document would be a governed-schema change. AC-1 does not require it. If @architect finds it necessary for GA, @po places it separately.
forArchitect.alsoRule: Whether the GuidedBridgeIntegrationTest mounted-rule cases can be expressed through governed region readGrants on the bridge fixture page. If they cannot, which cases are dropped by name.

forR14: Add the @architect-ruled refusal to s3-cutover.patch: guidedConfig.ts MOUNTED_KEYS/type, guidedMain.ts:24, createGuidedServer option check, and runtime rules: [] if ruled.
Tests: a mounted read-granting rule gives CONFIGURATION_DENIED. A static check that the entry point no longer passes `rules`. Re-point studio-runner/test/run/guidedMain.test.ts:12.
Record the hunk and the tests in r14/ledger.json s3CutoverPatch.
forB14OrItOwner: In the same S3 unit (AR-2 S-10, C2b SC-6): move GuidedBridgeIntegrationTest's mounted-rule read cases to governed readGrants in the frozen context, or drop them by name. Remove the `rules` key from the worker.json written by GuidedBridgeIntegrationTest, GuidedPlanningIntegrationTest and GuidedPublicationReplayIT (:15868) if the key itself is refused.
qaOracles: (1) A mounted config with a permittedBusinessData or nonsecretApproved rule gives CONFIGURATION_DENIED, and the worker does not start. If structuralOnly is kept, that rule is accepted and grants no read; otherwise any `rules` key is refused.
(2) On a governed context with no read grants, an element whose data-testid matches a would-be rule exports structuralOnly, and a read on it is READ_REFUSED.
(3) The re-pointed bridge IT read cases pass only through governed readGrants.
fallback: If @architect rules that this cannot land in S3, it stays a named AC-1 obligation of OBS-014 that blocks OBS-010 release readiness. It is never moved to the R-2 follow-up.
